developments.title: Curated benchmark for LLM psychological profiling and theory of mind
detail: A new benchmark has been curated to test large language models on psychological profiling, theory of mind understanding, and their ability to function as a psychological counselor.
The benchmark provides a concrete evaluation suite for measuring how well LLMs can perform tasks that require nuanced mental state reasoning and empathetic interaction.
developments.why_it_matters: The benchmark gives researchers and developers an immediate tool to assess LLMs' capabilities in psychological domains, informing model improvement and safety considerations.

developments.title: Cursor‑powered Git‑at‑Scale Rust binary released as open source
detail: A Rust binary implementing “Git at Scale” was open‑sourced, allowing users to point it at any S3‑compatible object store. It uses write‑ahead logging (WAL) and content‑addressable storage (CAS) primitives and requires no additional datastore. The tool also supports bundle‑uri, enabling fast download of large monorepos as a chain of static bundles with a familiar UX.
developments.why_it_matters: It lets teams clone massive repositories from S3 storage quickly and with minimal infrastructure, reducing clone times and storage overhead for large codebases.

developments.title: Pi v0.84.3 released with Windows PowerShell support and faster startup
detail: Pi version 0.84.3 has been announced, adding an optional PowerShell tool that can be enabled on Windows.
The update changes the bundling process, allowing the application to launch noticeably quicker on most systems.
These changes are documented in the release announcement posted by Pi.
developments.why_it_matters: Windows users of Pi can now enable PowerShell and experience faster application startup, improving overall usability.

developments.title: fast-rlm adds CLI support for coding agents to run RLM experiments
detail: The fast-rlm tool now includes a command‑line interface that allows coding agents to execute REPL‑based RLM experiments. It grants Codex/CC access to the REPL with the prompt supplied as a context variable, and agent responses are run directly within the REPL. The feature operates without API usage fees and supports ACP, while still permitting agents to fall back to traditional mode if they choose.
developments.why_it_matters: Developers can run RLM workflows locally via the CLI without incurring external API costs, streamlining experimentation and reducing reliance on cloud services.

developments.title: Claude Code vs Factory AI Droid Harness Benchmark Shows Faster, Cheaper Results
detail: Sarah Chieng reported that the same Claude Opus 4.6 model was run in two different coding harnesses—Claude Code and Factory AI Droid—to clone Excalidraw from scratch and implement its key interactions.

Factory AI Droid completed the task in 8 minutes with 20 tool calls costing $1.60, while Claude Code took 19 minutes, made 40 tool calls, and cost $1.87, demonstrating that the harness can significantly affect performance and cost.
developments.why_it_matters: The result highlights that choice of integration harness can double execution speed and halve costs for Claude agents, informing developers on efficient deployment strategies.

developments.title: Luma's Software Factory Design Patterns Episode
detail: The episode outlines key interfaces in a modern software factory, compares options for acquiring versus building components, and describes two layers of the harness equation that affect performance and cost. It also highlights which components builders should retain ownership of.
developments.why_it_matters: The discussion gives builders a concrete roadmap for structuring AI‑powered development pipelines, enabling more efficient tool selection and cost control.

developments.title: bananastand CLI evaluates RAM and storage value on Linux
detail: The open‑source bananastand project provides a tiny command‑line tool that reports the current monetary worth of a system's RAM and storage devices. It runs on Linux only and can be invoked directly from the terminal.
The tool is hosted on GitHub (github.com/dbreunig/bananastand) where the source code and usage instructions are publicly available.
developments.why_it_matters: Linux users can quickly assess the financial value of their hardware, aiding budgeting or resale decisions without leaving the command line.

external_links.title: GitHub - dbreunig/bananastand: “There's always money in the banana stand.” · GitHub

developments.title: Greg Pstrucha says Junior filters relevant pull-request alerts and pre-reviews them
detail: Greg Pstrucha said he configured Junior to notify him when pull requests relevant to him or his repositories are created, replacing an all-or-nothing notification flow. He added that Junior can also pre-review those pull requests. Junior's site describes it as a tool that investigates issues, gathers company context, and takes action with connected tools from a Slack thread.
developments.why_it_matters: The setup gives Pstrucha targeted pull-request alerts instead of requiring him to monitor every repository, while adding a pre-review step.

developments.title: Conductor MCP Enables Claude, Codex, and Cursor Agents to Manage Cloud Sessions
detail: The Conductor MCP has been introduced as a new tool that allows Claude, Codex, and Cursor agents to operate alongside human users. It provides the necessary utilities for agents to create and manage cloud sessions, and access is granted via an OAuth‑authenticated link.
Installation instructions are supplied in a get‑started text file, directing users to add the Conductor MCP via the provided URL.
developments.why_it_matters: Agents can now orchestrate cloud sessions directly through Conductor MCP, expanding their operational capabilities in real‑time environments.

developments.title: Codemod launches ast‑grep‑based structural code search for agents
detail: Codemod announced new grep features that use ast‑grep to perform structural, syntax‑aware searches across both public and internal repositories.
The service lets AI agents search code by shape rather than plain text or regex, enabling more precise code understanding and automated refactoring.
developments.why_it_matters: Agents can now locate and manipulate code patterns at scale, reducing manual effort and improving the reliability of automated code changes.

developments.title: Vercel AI Gateway Offers Zero Markup and Volume Discounts
detail: Vercel announced that its AI Gateway now charges zero markup on listed model prices and provides custom volume discounts for customers with high token usage.

The discounts are applied as reduced token spend rates, with models already priced below list for every team and optional zero‑fee ACH payments for large‑scale usage, as detailed in the Vercel AI Gateway pricing documentation.
developments.why_it_matters: The zero‑markup pricing and volume discounts lower the cost of running AI workloads on Vercel, allowing teams to scale inference and experimentation without additional fees.

developments.title: OpenProse workflow file turns policy into an agent‑readable document
detail: OpenProse bundles the entire funnel into a single workflow file, converting policy definitions into a document that an AI agent must follow. The file includes queue rules, stop conditions, and other execution parameters, allowing agents to operate with a clear, unified policy set.
By consolidating these elements, OpenProse simplifies the deployment and management of agents in cloud environments, reducing the need for multiple configuration artifacts.
developments.why_it_matters: This unified workflow enables faster setup of policy‑driven agents, improving reliability and maintainability for teams running AI agents in the cloud.

developments.title: opencode2 Initial Documentation Released
detail: The opencode2 team announced the release of initial documentation for building with opencode2. The docs cover plugins, TUI plugins, an API client, embedding support, and Cloudflare integration, giving developers concrete guidance to start using the platform.
developments.why_it_matters: Official docs lower the barrier for developers to adopt opencode2, enabling immediate integration of plugins and cloud services.

developments.title: OpenAI to reinstate 5-hour usage cap on ChatGPT Plus, Work, and Codex plans
detail: Tibo announced that the 5-hour usage limit will be reinstated for ChatGPT Plus accounts across ChatGPT Work and Codex beginning the following day.

He framed the cap as necessary to smooth compute load so the plan can remain generous in weekly usage, and to prevent casual and new Plus users from accidentally exhausting their weekly allotment in a single burst and then being confused by the experience.
The 5-hour limit will remain disabled for Pro $100 and Pro $200 subscriptions over the upcoming months.
developments.why_it_matters: Plus subscribers will face an enforced per-5-hour cap that limits how much ChatGPT they can consume in short windows and changes day-to-day usage patterns, while Pro $100 and Pro $200 subscribers are explicitly exempt from this change.
